jobs.occupation: Senior Manager, Global Labor Management - Retail Operations
jobs.description:
Do you want to shape the future of workforce management in one of the world's largest jewelry brands?

At Pandora, we're accelerating our Retail Excellence agenda to deliver world-class customer experiences across our global store network. As our new Senior Manager, Global Labour Management, you will play a pivotal role in defining and driving the global labour strategy that enables our stores to operate efficiently while supporting business growth and exceptional customer service.

Based at our global headquarters in Copenhagen, you will work closely with senior stakeholders across Retail Operations, Finance, HR, Data & Analytics, and Digital & Technology to help optimize workforce planning and labour productivity across markets worldwide.

Your Role

As the global expert within labour management, you will lead the development and execution of Pandora's workforce management strategy while ensuring alignment across our international retail organization.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• 
Developing and evolving Pandora's global labour strategy to support productivity, profitability, and sales growth.

• 
Partnering with Digital & Technology and Data & Analytics teams to enhance workforce management tools and capabilities, including our workforce management platform, Plan.dora.

• 
Driving the evolution of labour budgeting processes in close collaboration with Finance, HR, and local commercial teams.

• 
Leveraging data and insights to identify opportunities for improving workforce productivity, scheduling efficiency, and store performance.

• 
Establishing global workforce management standards, processes, policies, and KPIs.

• 
Supporting and coaching local workforce management teams across markets to strengthen capabilities and drive adoption of best practices.

• 
Leading continuous improvement initiatives and identifying opportunities to leverage new technologies and AI-powered workforce management solutions.

• 
Ensuring compliance with labour regulations, workforce management policies, and scheduling standards across markets.

What We're Looking For

We imagine that you bring a combination of strategic thinking, operational excellence, and strong stakeholder management skills.

You likely have:

• 
Significant experience within Retail Operations and workforce or labour management.

• 
Experience from retail, fashion, beauty, lifestyle, or other customer-facing industries.

• 
A strong understanding of store operations and the drivers behind labour productivity and customer experience.

• 
Experience leading teams and driving change across complex organizations.

• 
Exposure to international and matrix environments, ideally within a multi-country or global organization.

• 
Strong analytical capabilities and the ability to translate data into business decisions.

• 
Experience with workforce management platforms and scheduling solutions. Knowledge of Dayforce is an advantage.

• 
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence at all organizational levels.

• 
Fluency in English.

What You'll Get

This is a unique opportunity to build and mature a global capability that directly impacts Pandora's retail performance worldwide.

You'll join a highly collaborative and international environment where you can:

• 
Influence strategic decisions across a global retail network.

• 
Drive transformation and innovation within workforce management.

• 
Work with senior leaders across multiple business functions.

• 
Develop solutions that directly contribute to store profitability and operational excellence.

• 
Help shape the future way of working for thousands of store colleagues around the world.

Did we get your attention?

If you see yourself in the position and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible.

You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

About Pandora

Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

Recognised by the Financial Times as one of Europe’s Best Workplaces and ranked #1 among Danish companies, Pandora is committed to building an inclusive and diverse workplace. We believe that reflecting the diversity of society in how we engage with our customers is essential to fulfilling our purpose: to give a voice to people’s loves. We are dedicated to nurturing a culture where everyone feels respected, valued

Global Business Services (GBS) Strategy Manager

• Full-time

• Field of interest: Technology, Transformation & Data

• Level of hire: Experienced hire

Company Description

With more than 2,700 employees, Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit, Tax, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, Technology, and Transformations.

About our team

Finance Transformation is part of Deloitte’s consulting practice and consists of 350 dedicated consultants who work within all aspects of the CFO area and engage with clients to advise, transform, optimize, and operate the finance function. We have private and public as well as national and international clients across different industries and of different sizes, and we work with the lion’s share of C25 companies and public institutions.

Global Business Services (GBS) is an integral part of Deloitte’s Finance Transformation practice. The GBS team is dedicated to helping organizations transform their business operations, driving higher efficiency, effectiveness, and agility. By leveraging a comprehensive suite of services, the GBS practice supports clients in optimizing shared services, outsourcing, and global business service models to create value and enhance performance. We work in the full lifecycle of projects from strategy to design and implementation.

We are seeking an experienced and skilled Manager to join our Global Business Services (GBS) team. The ideal candidate has experience in setting up shared services organizations and a deep understanding of multi-functional GBS operations. Experience with the interplay of technology and process design in this context is preferred. This role will be pivotal in driving strategic business transformation initiatives, building effective governance structures, implementing new capabilities globally and optimizing functional processes leveraging the latest technologies.

Job Description

As a GBS Strategy Manager, you will lead large complex engagements for some of the world's biggest organizations. In this role, you will architect future-ready GBS strategies, drive end-to-end finance process transformations, and leverage cutting-edge AI technologies to enable growth and value creation. You will be responsible for leading business model transformations, setting up shared services or outsourcing solutions, and leveraging a commercial mindset to position and scale innovation. You will identify, design, and implement shared services solutions aimed at driving operational effectiveness, cost efficiencies, and organizational agility.

In this role, you will make an impact by:

• Identifying key client business issues and architecting end-to-end finance process transformations (e.g., R2R, O2C, P2P)

• Driving business development by responding to Requests for Proposal (RFPs) and pitching strategic solutions with a strong commercial mindset

• Evaluating and deploying innovative technologies, including GenAI and intelligent automation, to elevate client digital maturity and process performance

• Determining which techniques, delivery models, and emerging tech are best suited to serving each client's unique addressable needs

• Developing recommendations for the client in the context of overall engagement

• Leading day-to-day team activities and effectively overseeing the quality of deliverables

• Managing diverse small and big teams

Qualifications

Ideally, you have:

• Around 6-9 years of relevant experience in the GBS, Shared Services and/or Business Process Outsourcing, as well as good understanding of finance processes

• 3+ years of Direct people management experience

• Bachelor's degree from an accredited university

• Fluency in Danish is a big plus

What you bring to the team:

• Experience with multiple GBS pillars including, but not limited to HR, IT, Finance, Procurement, Commercial Operations, Legal

• Extensive project experience within the Shared Services, Outsourcing and/or Offshoring industry, or back-office functional optimization

• Experience with service delivery model strategy, design, implementation & optimization for multi-functional or single-function entities

• Strong critical thinking, analytical and problem-solving skills

• Exceptional interpersonal, team-building and oral and written communication skills; outstanding integrity, initiative, creativity, and passion

• Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, ambiguous, dynamic environment and manage multiple priorities.

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we still encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can make an impact on our team.

Additional Information

Do you want to be part of our team?

Click the "I am interested" button above if you are ready to join our team.

Send your CV by 30.11.2026. We process applications and arrange interviews continually, so we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

Who we are

Better Collective is a global digital sports media group on a mission to excite sports fans and build communities worldwide. We operate at the intersection of sports, media, technology, betting and prediction markets. With brands like FUTBIN, HLTV, Action Network, Playmaker HQ, VegasInsider, Bolavip, FutbolSites and more, we engage 450+ million monthly users worldwide. We combine the scale of a corporation with the speed and mindset of a startup.

About the role

We’re looking for an AI Engineer to join Better Collective and help us build, test and improve AI-driven solutions and automated workflows for the publishing business. You will collaborate with QA, product, editorial and production teams to build proofs-of-concept, MVPs and scalable solutions across content, video, image and data processing.

What you’ll do

• 
Build, run and evaluate POCs and MVPs, especially for automated content creation and AI-assisted publishing workflows.

• 
Develop practical AI solutions using LLMs, APIs, orchestration frameworks, retrieval systems, automation pipelines and agentic workflows.

• 
Experiment quickly with new tools, frameworks, models and technical approaches.

• 
Translate business needs into reliable technical solutions with a focus on speed and measurable value.

What we’re looking for

Must have

• 
Hands-on experience with AI/ML tools, LLMs and API integrations.

• 
Experience with frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or similar.

• 
Strong programming skills in Python and/or TypeScript.

• 
Ability to code, debug, integrate APIs and design AI-powered workflows.

• 
Experience building and evaluating practical AI solutions.

Nice to have

• 
Prompt engineering, model evaluation and output validation.

• 
Workflow automation and agentic systems experience.

Important: This is not a no-code or low-code automation role. Tools such as Make, Zapier, Lovable, or Bolt can be useful, but they are not enough on their own. We’re looking for someone comfortable working directly with code and using AI as part of a serious engineering workflow.

About the hiring process

As part of the final hiring process, candidates must present a project, prototype, workflow, or pipeline they personally built that actively uses AI. It should demonstrate:

• 
The problem being solved and how AI was used.

• 
The tools, models, APIs, frameworks, or coding agents involved.

• 
The approach taken to build it.

• 
What worked, what didn’t and what they changed.

• 
The final result and its practical value.

Projects built only with no-code or low-code tools will not meet this requirement unless they also include clear coding, API integration, or technical system design. This is intended to demonstrate hands-on ability, technical curiosity and independent execution.

jobs.description:
We are looking for an analytical profile with in-depth Rewards experience to join our Global Rewards & People Analytics team.

About the team

Our team brings together expertise across Global Rewards, Mobility, People Analytics, People Technology & Data, and Danish Payroll & Benefits.

In Rewards, we are responsible for the design, governance and continuous development of our global reward programmes and frameworks. You will be a key partner to the Senior Director Global Rewards & People Analytics on Executive Rewards, supporting analyses, market insights, presentations, remuneration governance and the development of future reward solutions.

“We are an ambitious and engaged team focused on developing solutions that are relevant, engaging and aligned with business needs, while ensuring successful implementation across the organisation”, says Wandunia Pontoppidan, Senior Director, Global Rewards.

The job

You will build a strong network across the organisation and work closely with colleagues across functions and countries from specialists to people partners and senior leaders.

In preparation for our Remuneration Committee meetings, you will partner closely with Senior Director, Global Rewards & People Analytics on executive remuneration and the ongoing evolution of our variable pay programmes. You will analyse current practices, assess market trends and alternative approaches, and develop recommendations that help ensure our reward programmes remain competitive, effective and aligned with our strategic priorities.

In close collaboration with Reward colleagues, people partners and business leaders, you will be responsible for:

•    Supporting Remuneration Committee activities, including benchmarking, analytics, presentation materials and recommendations related to executive remuneration.

•    Supporting annual Executive Leadership Team reward reviews and reporting activities.

•    Reviewing and designing short and long-term incentive programmes, including implementation planning and change communications.

•    Partnering with leaders and people partners on position evaluations and salary recommendations for new hires and promotions at ‘Director’ level and above.

•    Conducting organisational and remuneration reviews and contributing to projects that strengthen our reward offerings across geographies.

•    Contributing to country benchmarking and annual salary review activities, including salary range development and budgeting during peak periods.

You will work with senior stakeholders and translate complex information into clear decision-making material. You will challenge the status quo and balance thorough analysis with pragmatic solutions. Drawing on data, market insights and external trends, you will help shape reward solutions that support both business priorities and the employee experience.

What you bring

We are looking for someone who can build credibility and influence through strong relationships, sound judgement and thoughtful communication. You are confident in your expertise, while remaining curious, open to feedback and keen to learn from others. You are ambitious and always strive for great results together with your team and colleagues, and you know how to balance high quality with timely deliveries.

You understand the critical link between reward design, people data and technology. You are comfortable working with people data structures, governance and system implications, ensuring that reward frameworks can be translated into practical, compliant and efficient solutions across platforms.

Given the nature of the role, you handle sensitive information with discretion and sound judgement, and confidentiality is a natural part of how you work.

Qualifications and personality

We expect that you:

•    Hold a relevant Masters’ degree

•    Have +5 years of experience working in Rewards in a global context.

•    Have experience working with executive remuneration and various long-term incentive instruments.

•    Possess strong stakeholder relations and collaboration skills

•    Have a curious and analytical mindset, and the ability to comprehend complex data sets.

•    Can convert data into findings and recommendations through simple and appealing visuals.

•    Are structured, organised and have a strong eye for detail

•    Are strong in Excel and PowerPoint and can apply AI

•    Communicate fluently in English, both verbally and in writing

We offer

This position offers a global perspective, with collaboration across our 42 countries.  You will gain exposure to the full Rewards agenda, with a particular focus on Executive Remuneration and short and long-term incentive programmes. The role combines analytical depth with stakeholder engagement, translating complex data into insights and decision materials for senior stakeholders.

Our culture is one of trust, fun and creativity, with a strong focus on quality, compliance and process optimization. We are part of the People & Culture organization and work out of our HQ in Denmark.

jobs.occupation: Senior Backend Developer, Product and Data
jobs.description:
What we are building

Someone researching a purchase might start in ChatGPT, compare options in Perplexity, run a Google search, then go back to an AI assistant to decide. The companies being compared have little idea where they show up in that chain or what gets said about them, and very few can measure it today.

We build the infrastructure that measures it. Every platform we track changes under us, and none of them offers a feed, so we collect the data ourselves. Three products run on it:

• AccuRanker is the rank tracking and SEO analytics platform. Rankings, competitor movement, keyword research, dashboards, forecasting.

• AccuLLM tracks brand visibility inside ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overview, and AI Mode.

• AccuSERP is a search data API we sell to other companies in the industry. On a normal day that means 27 billion rows inserted, 85 million web requests collected, 80 million background jobs run, and 64 million analytical queries served. Eight people build and run all of it.

This job is on the product side: the backend, the data models, and the query paths that run on top of what we collect.

What you will work on

• Build features across AccuRanker and AccuLLM: Django APIs, background jobs, and the data models behind them.

• Design ClickHouse schemas and query paths, and keep the 64 million daily analytical queries fast as the data grows.

• Work across Postgres and ClickHouse, and decide what lives where.

• Own services end to end, from design through deployment to how they behave in production.

• Take features into the React frontend if you want to. Fullstack is welcome, not required.

What you bring

Must have:

• Python and a major web framework (we run Django and Celery), or equivalent depth in another stack.

• Database and API design. Schemas, indexes, migrations, and APIs that hold up under load.

• Comfort in Linux and close to production. Debugging incidents, understanding system behavior, improving observability, making services more reliable.

• Ownership and initiative. You take a problem, you decide how to solve it, and you follow through.

Good to have:

• React and TypeScript, for the optional frontend part of the job.

• ClickHouse or another columnar store at scale.

• Kafka.

• AI agents in production. Tool and context design, structured output and evals.

• Data infrastructure at scale. The ingestion, storage, and query-performance problems our numbers imply.

Who does well here

People who set a high standard for their own work, and who care about performance, reliability, cost, and operational simplicity.

You own a feature end to end, from idea to production. You can make progress while the problem is still half defined, and a month after it ships, you are still the one who cares about it.

You move fast when speed is what the problem needs, and you know when stability, safety, and maintainability matter more.

This field moves fast right now. We expect you to read, try things, and form your own view of what is worth using, without waiting to be told what is new.

The job is wide. In one week you might tune a query, ship a customer-facing feature, and design an agent.

This role is not for you if you want a roadmap handed to you, a narrow technical scope, or a large team around you. We are small, the problems change, and you will often be the person deciding both what to build and what “done” means.

AI at AccuRanker

AI is a big part of the product and of how we build it. AccuLLM sends queries to LLMs all day, customers use our MCP server, and agents and tool design are real engineering problems here.

Being effective with coding agents is becoming a core engineering skill, and it is part of this job. You should be good at giving agents the right context, breaking work into pieces they can execute well, reviewing what they produce, and knowing when to take over yourself. The bar is more high-quality engineering done without outsourcing your understanding and judgment, which is a different thing from using AI a lot.

How we work

• You own services, not tickets. You decide how to solve the problem, make the tradeoffs, and deploy it yourself.

• We ship many times a day. A change can go from idea to production the same day.

• We argue about designs, in writing and in the room. Correctness, cost, and latency are worth arguing about out loud.

• We share what we know and help each other own unfamiliar parts of the system.

What we offer

• Salary set individually on skills and experience.

• Pension, health insurance, flexible working hours, and paid parental leave.

• Hardware of your choosing.

• Office in central Aarhus on Åboulevarden, top floors, panoramic views over the city. The role is on-site, with hybrid options planned for later this year.

• Great lunch.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note to pet@accuranker.com, in Danish or English.

We review applications as they come in and hire as soon as we find the right person, so send yours when it is ready.

Questions about the role are welcome. Call our CTO, Peter Emil Tybirk, on +45 61 41 77 41.

jobs.occupation: Senior Backend Developer, Data Collection and Infrastructure
jobs.description:
What we are building

Someone researching a purchase might start in ChatGPT, compare options in Perplexity, run a Google search, then go back to an AI assistant to decide. The companies being compared have little idea where they show up in that chain or what gets said about them, and very few can measure it today.

We build the infrastructure that measures it. Every platform we track changes under us, and none of them offers a feed, so we collect the data ourselves. The collection is the hard part, and it is most of this job. Three products run on it:

• AccuRanker is the rank tracking and SEO analytics platform. Rankings, competitor movement, keyword research, dashboards, forecasting.

• AccuLLM tracks brand visibility inside ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overview, and AI Mode.

• AccuSERP is a search data API we sell to other companies in the industry.

On a normal day that means 27 billion rows inserted, 85 million web requests collected, 80 million background jobs run, and 64 million analytical queries served. Eight people build and run all of it.

What you will work on

• Scale the collection and ingestion pipeline behind those numbers. Drive down cost and latency per request as volume grows.

• Add new search surfaces as they appear, and keep the ones we already cover working when they change shape.

• Design storage and query paths for very large time series data, across columnar and relational stores.

• Own services end to end, from design through deployment to how they behave in production.

What you bring

Must have:

• Distributed systems fundamentals. Queues, workers, backpressure, etc.

• Comfort in Linux and close to production. Debugging incidents, understanding system behavior, improving observability, making services more reliable.

• Ownership and initiative. You take a problem, you decide how to solve it, and you follow through.

Good to have:

• The network layer in depth. Connection lifecycle, timeouts and retries, TLS, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

• ClickHouse or another columnar store at scale.

• AI agents in production. Tool and context design, structured output and evals.

• Large scale web scraping or browser automation.

• Kafka.

• Python and its common frameworks (Django, Celery, pandas/polars). Our stack runs mostly on Python, but it is not a must if the fundamentals are strong.

• Data infrastructure at scale. The ingestion, storage, and query-performance problems our numbers imply.

Who does well here

People who set a high standard for their own work, and who care about performance, reliability, cost, and operational simplicity.

You own a feature end to end, from idea to production. You can make progress while the problem is still half defined, and a month after it ships, you are still the one who cares about it.

You move fast when speed is what the problem needs, and you know when stability, safety and maintainability matter more.

This field moves fast right now. We expect you to read, try things, and form your own view of what is worth using, without waiting to be told what is new.

The job is wide. In one week you might tune a database, debug a proxy network, and design an agent.

This role is not for you if you want a roadmap handed to you, a narrow technical scope, or a large team around you. We are small, the problems change, and you will often be the person deciding both what to build and what “done” means.

AI at AccuRanker

AI is a big part of the product and of how we build it. AccuLLM sends queries to LLMs all day, customers use our MCP server, and agents and tool design are real engineering problems here.

Being effective with coding agents is becoming a core engineering skill, and it is part of this job. You should be good at giving agents the right context, breaking work into pieces they can execute well, reviewing what they produce, and knowing when to take over yourself. The bar is more high-quality engineering done without outsourcing your understanding and judgment, which is a different thing from using AI a lot.

How we work

• You own services, not tickets. You decide how to solve the problem, make the tradeoffs, and deploy it yourself.

• We ship many times a day. A change can go from idea to production the same day.

• We argue about designs, in writing and in the room. Correctness, cost, and latency are worth arguing about out loud.

• We share what we know and help each other own unfamiliar parts of the system.

What we offer

• Salary set individually on skills and experience.

• Pension, health insurance, flexible working hours, and paid parental leave.

• Hardware of your choosing.

• Office in central Aarhus on Åboulevarden, top floors, panoramic views over the city. The role is on-site, with hybrid options planned for later this year.

• Great lunch.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note to pet@accuranker.com, in Danish or English.

We review applications as they come in and hire as soon as we find the right person, so send yours when it is ready.

Questions about the role are welcome. Call our CTO, Peter Emil Tybirk, on +45 61 41 77 41.
